title: Why a Submitted Form Can Still Lose a Lead
description: Draft for human review. A fictional, visual walkthrough of a safer web-form workflow; it contains no client metrics or claimed results.
hook: The form says “Submitted.” So why is there no lead?

scenes.voiceover: The form says “Submitted.” So why is there no lead?
scenes.subtitle: Submitted—but no lead?
scenes.visual_prompt: Vertical 9:16 motion graphic of a generic web form changing to a green Submitted state, followed by an empty lead inbox. Add a persistent small label: FICTIONAL DEMO. No brands, logos, analytics, or real customer data.

scenes.voiceover: In this fictional demo, success appears before the server confirms storage.
scenes.subtitle: Success appeared too early
scenes.visual_prompt: Vertical 9:16 fictional system diagram. Animate Browser to Server to Lead Store. Show the success checkmark appearing while the Server-to-Lead-Store connection is still pending. Label the interface FICTIONAL DEMO.

scenes.voiceover: Then a notification fails. The visitor leaves, while the team sees nothing.
scenes.subtitle: The notification fails
scenes.visual_prompt: Vertical 9:16 animation: notification branch turns red with a clear Failed label, visitor icon exits, and the team inbox remains empty. Keep FICTIONAL DEMO visible. Use only generic icons.

scenes.voiceover: Use a safer sequence: validate on the server, then save the lead first.
scenes.subtitle: Validate → Save first
scenes.visual_prompt: Vertical 9:16 step diagram with large numbered blocks: 1 Server validation, 2 Save lead. Animate a green confirmation moving through both steps in order. Mark as RECOMMENDED PATTERN and FICTIONAL DEMO.

scenes.voiceover: In this pattern, repeat submissions with one request ID become one request.
scenes.subtitle: One ID, one request
scenes.visual_prompt: Vertical 9:16 diagram showing two retry arrows carrying the same fictional request ID into a single request record. Do not display code, personal data, or real identifiers. Label FICTIONAL DEMO.

scenes.voiceover: After storage succeeds, show confirmation. Run notifications as retryable follow-up tasks.
scenes.subtitle: Save → Confirm → Notify
scenes.visual_prompt: Vertical 9:16 ordered flow: Lead Stored gets a green check, then Visitor Confirmation, then a separate Notification Queue with a retry arrow. Use large readable labels and a FICTIONAL DEMO tag.

scenes.voiceover: Log each step and flag failures. Map this path before your next launch.
scenes.subtitle: Log, flag, review
scenes.visual_prompt: Vertical 9:16 closing card with a simple checklist: Validate, Save, Confirm, Notify, Log. Highlight Map the full path. Add Draft for human review and FICTIONAL DEMO in small but readable text.

cta: Map your form’s full path—from Submit to stored lead—before your next launch.

source_notes.claim: The failure sequence shown in the video is a fictional demonstration, not a client case or reported result.
source_notes.note: Provided evidence defines the example as a fictional demonstration built in Content Factory.

source_notes.claim: The validate, save, confirm, notify, and log sequence is presented as a workflow design recommendation.
source_notes.note: No performance statistics, guarantees, client outcomes, or external factual claims are included. Draft for human review.
